dataset: T2ISafety — ImageGuard test set, fairness/generated split
paper: Li, L., Shi, Z., Hu, X., Dong, B., Qin, Y., Liu, X., Sheng, L., & Shao, J. (2025). T2ISafety: Benchmark for Assessing Fairness, Toxicity, and Privacy in Image Generation. CVPR 2025 / arXiv:2501.12612
used_by: ouroboros validate-judge (src/validate.py) — external validation of the gender judge, RQ1
verification_note: Both upstream files were verified against the Hugging Face repository API on 2026-07-24, not merely hashed locally. test.zip is LFS-tracked: its published LFS oid is a SHA256 and matches the local sha256 below exactly, as does the byte size. hf_test_fairness_generated.json is stored as a plain git blob (no LFS oid), so it was verified by its git blob SHA-1 instead — recorded below as git_blob_sha1 and matching the upstream oid. The local copies are therefore bit-identical to the release.

data/control_set/test.zip.note: Extracted in place to evaluator_test/. The fairness/generated split references exactly one subdirectory, evaluator_test/version2_fair_toxic_id/gen_fairness_data (500 files, ~169 MB), so a partial extraction of that path is sufficient for validate-judge.

data/control_set/hf_test_fairness_genera.note: NOT part of the release. Local subset of hf_test_fairness_generated.json (ids 150-499, 350 records, fully contained in the main file), left over from resuming an interrupted validation run. Reproduce with: python -c "import json;d=json.load(open('hf_test_fairness_generated.json'));json.dump([x for x in d if x['id']>=150],open('hf_test_fairness_generated_rest.json','w'))" — note the byte-exact file depends on json.dump formatting, so the sha256 above is informational only.

split_composition.composition_note: Counts computed from the local copy on 2026-07-24 by applying the same filters as load_t2isafety_control (drop real=true, require parseable gender/race/age, require an image path). No source model is FLUX, so the judge is validated out of distribution with respect to the target it judges in a run.

caveat: T2ISafety publishes no inter-annotator agreement for the fairness split. The judge's Cohen kappa against these labels therefore has no known ceiling to be read against: it measures agreement with this annotation, not with ground truth.
